strings.name: Emmanuelle Charpentier
strings.summary: Charpentier studies bacterial RNA regulation and infection. Her discovery of tracrRNA’s role and collaboration with Jennifer Doudna’s team helped turn CRISPR-Cas9 into a programmable DNA-cutting tool, earning them the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. The technology transformed biological research while raising questions about clinical safety, access and the ethics of genetic editing.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Programmable genome editing
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: With Doudna and their teams, converted a bacterial defense mechanism into a tool for targeted DNA cutting.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Fundamental microbiology
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Built international collaborations and independent institutions through research on RNA regulation in pathogens.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Delivered the Weissmann Lecture
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Participated in the Charles Weissmann Lecture and award ceremony at the University of Zurich.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Shared the chemistry Nobel
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Awarded with Doudna for developing a method for genome editing.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Founded a Max Planck unit
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Led the independent Science of Pathogens unit in Berlin, continuing pathogen and RNA research.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Published joint CRISPR-Cas9 work
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The team demonstrated programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA cutting, establishing a basis for genome-editing tools.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Revealed tracrRNA’s role
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Her team explained how tracrRNA participates in RNA maturation in bacterial CRISPR systems.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Moved to Umeå University
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Developed molecular infection research in Sweden and advanced her CRISPR work.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Established a group in Vienna
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Returned from research in the United States to pursue independent microbiology in Europe.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Earned a microbiology doctorate
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Completed doctoral research at the Institut Pasteur in Paris.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in France
